summary.headline: Jyoti CNC Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit by INR67 crore Huron POCM reversal; standalone revenue up 13% to INR599 crore, capacity constrained.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue rose 13% YoY to INR599 crore with EBITDA margin of 31.9%, while FY26 standalone revenue grew 20% to INR1,949 crore. Consolidated Q4 revenue was reported at INR599 crore after a INR67 crore revenue reversal at Huron, which management calls a deferment of POCM revenue pending export licences from an ongoing export-control investigation. Consolidated Q4 EBITDA was INR147 crore (24.6% margin) and PAT INR91 crore; FY26 consolidated PAT rose 6% to INR336 crore. Order book stood at INR4,732 crore, and the 10,000-machine capacity expansion (to 16,000 machines) is slated to start commercial operation around September 2026.

segments.name: Standalone India
segments.commentary: Q4 executed about 1,760 machines (management cited 1,750 in one answer); FY26 about 5,550 machines, with average realisation of INR35.62 lakh. Utilisation exceeded 100% in peak months.

segments.name: Huron (France, consolidated)
segments.commentary: Standalone Huron revenue (sold to parent) was INR25 crore in Q4 and INR248 crore in FY26, of which INR105 crore was intercompany. INR67 crore POCM revenue reversed in Q4 pending export licences; management expects INR300-350 crore normal level for FY27.

segments.name: End-sector mix FY26 revenue
segments.commentary: Aerospace and defence 39%, auto and auto components 26%, general engineering 23%, others including EMS and dies and moulds the balance.

segments.name: Order book mix (31 March 2026)
segments.commentary: Aerospace and defence 38%, auto and auto components 20%, general engineering 19%, EMS 4%, balance other sectors. FY26 order intake mix: aerospace 27%, auto 28%, general engineering 31%.

guidance_outlook: Capacity expansion of 10,000 machines (to 16,000 annual) on track to commence around September 2026 (Q2 FY27); management says it will update FY27 volume numbers in 3-4 months.
Management said it will not quantify FY27 execution; order book to be executed over 18-20 months.
Management expects ramp-up speed to rise 20-30% after new capacity starts; standalone machine target for FY27 not given.
Management expects consolidated EBITDA margin to stay around 25% plus, even as average machine price falls toward INR30 lakh at full utilisation of expanded capacity.
Management expects the INR67 crore reversal (c.INR40 crore margin) to be recognised once export licences are received; it is not assumed to be lost.
Price increase of about 2-3% on raw materials effective 1 May 2026 for new customers and orders.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity currently 6,000 machines per year across India and Huron; facilities ran above 100% utilisation in peak months.
Expansion to 16,000 machines per year; commercial operation targeted for September 2026 (Q2 FY27).
Debt rose by about INR300 crore in FY26 for capacity expansion; working capital debt rose INR45 crore; total debt about INR850-plus crore.
Huron capacity expansion completed in FY26 with about 25 manufacturing people added; new facilities from November, dispatches from new assembly expected August-September.
Management says the new capacity is fully fungible across general engineering, auto, dies and moulds, and aerospace.
demand_pricing: Order intake in Q4 FY26 above INR700 crore, led by auto and general engineering; FY26 order intake INR2,364 crore.
Management says it has been selective in order booking to match delivery obligations; customer inquiries rising.
Recent European orders include Ukraine (about 6 machines, c.INR70 crore, through Huron, requiring licences next year) and a French government order.
Pricing: management says it cannot pass through cost increases on existing orders, but raised prices for new orders from 1 May 2026.
Machine categories: up to INR50 lakh entry-level, INR50 lakh-2 crore mid-range, above INR2 crore high-end. Aerospace roughly 40% high-end; auto and general engineering mostly entry and mid-range.
Management cited more than 15,000 customers in India (up from 14,000 last year).

qa_highlights.question: Could the Huron reversal have been a provision rather than a revenue reversal, and when will the INR67 crore be recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a deferment, not a write-off, per auditors; revenue will be recognised once export licences are granted. No timeline given for the investigation; legal counsel retained.

qa_highlights.question: How will cash flow and working capital be managed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects working capital needs to fall as manufacturing cycles shorten with new capacity, and said cash flow turned positive in FY26 from negative in FY25. No CFO/EBITDA ratio was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the standalone 13% growth in Q4 due to capacity constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Q4 standalone executed about 1,750-1,760 machines, above 100% of capacity, which constrained growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY27 execution can be expected from the INR4,700 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify; said it will update in 3-4 months once capacity is in place. Execution period is 18-20 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EMS execution expected to be back-ended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EMS clients are still optimising capacity and investment in components has been slow; pace expected to pick up from September after new capacity starts.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Huron investigation affect India aerospace execution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the technology is Jyoti's own; of about INR800 crore aerospace and defence executed in FY26, around 75% was from India, and no slowdown is seen.

qa_highlights.question: Margin and realisation trend as machine volumes rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin will stay around 25% plus; it expects average machine price to fall toward INR30 lakh at full utilisation of 16,000 machines, while margin holds near 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Huron to be sold or can it grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management ruled out any sale of Huron and said it expects Huron normal revenue of INR300-350 crore in FY27, with execution strengthening from Q2.

risks_watch: Export-control investigation at Huron (French authorities): no timeline; management could not rule out 2-5 years for licences, so the INR67 crore reversal may stay unrecognised for long. Also a general manager at Huron has been suspended.

Margin dilution: standalone realisation fell to INR35.62 lakh (FY26) from around INR13 lakh margin per machine per analyst math; analysts questioned sustainability of 25% EBITDA margin as volumes rise.
EMS demand delays: EMS customers (including Tata Electronics) are optimising capacity, so FY27 H1 execution may be muted.
Working capital and debt: debt up about INR300 crore for expansion; execution cycle is long, and management expects cash flow to improve.
Commodity inflation: about 2-3% raw-material cost rise in two months; fixed-price contracts on existing orders cannot be passed through.
Macro: West Asia conflict and tariffs cited as risks to energy prices and supply chains.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, capacity and the 25% margin outlook, but evasive on the Huron investigation timeline, the licence timing, and FY27 volume or revenue numbers. Management repeatedly stressed the reversal is a deferment rather than a write-off.
key_quotes: This is not a write-off. This is a deferment and this deferment of revenue of a POCM.
We will not go down by 25%. We are at -- if you imagine this, even this event happened, and we have taken this all deferment on revenue and margin.
It has no material adverse impact on the company's operations, including order execution, exports, customer servicing or ongoing manufacturing activities.
